name: sol_am_dosa_1
description: Push-based fund distribution causing denial-of-service if a recipient reverts or blocks the transfer
question: The source file in `source` implements a function that iterates over multiple recipients and directly pushes ETH or tokens to each one (e.g., via call/transfer/send inside a loop) as part of distributing funds, withdrawals, or refunds, without allowing recipients to pull their own funds individually, such that a single recipient's failing or maliciously reverting receive/fallback logic can block or permanently halt the distribution for all other recipients, excluding cases where the function already isolates each transfer with try/catch or records failures without reverting the whole loop, and excluding single-recipient withdrawal functions where only the caller's own funds are transferred.
criteria: A distributeRewards() or batchWithdraw() function loops through an array of user addresses and calls payable(user).transfer(amount) or call{value: amount} for each, reverting the entire loop if any single transfer fails
A refund mechanism sends ETH directly to multiple bidders/participants in a for loop using .send() or .call(), with no fallback path for a blocked recipient
A payout function pushes ERC20 tokens or ETH to a list of stored addresses during finalize()/closeAuction(), where one recipient's contract can revert on receipt and stop all subsequent payouts

A contract owner or admin-controlled function force-sends funds to users in bulk without a per-user pull-based withdraw() alternative, allowing a single griefing address to indefinitely block the whole batch
